lessons.title: Personality
lessons.theme: Personality traits, character, to be adjectives

grammar_details.focus: Personality Adjectives & Asking What is someone like?

rules.formula: What is + Subject + like? -> Subject + be + personality adjective
examples: What is your friend like? He is very kind and patient.
What are they like? They are brave and helpful.
He is not selfish or rude.
She is never careless.

rules: Combine personality adjectives with 'and' or 'but' (kind and patient, clever but a little quiet).

vocab_development.rules: kind vs cruel, brave vs coward, generous vs selfish, patient vs impatient, neat vs messy, quiet vs talkative, hard-working vs lazy.
examples: patient vs impatient
neat vs messy

see_also.topic: Prefix im- and in- in Personality Adjectives
see_also.rules: patient -> impatient, polite -> impolite, active -> inactive.

lessons.title: Travel
lessons.theme: Travel, airport, train station, booking hotel

grammar_details.focus: Present Continuous for Arranged Future & Travel Routines

rules.formula: Subject + am/is/are + V-ing + future time expression
examples: We are traveling to Isfahan next Monday.
He is taking the train tomorrow morning.

rules.formula: Where are you going? / How are you traveling?
examples: How are you traveling? We are traveling by plane.
Are you booking a hotel online? Yes, I am.

rules: State departure point, destination, transport mode, and travel companion clearly.

vocab_development.rules: ticket, passport, boarding pass, luggage, baggage, flight, terminal, train station, booking, passenger, timetable.
examples: boarding pass
train ticket

see_also.topic: Prepositions with Transport: by vs on/in
see_also.rules: by train, by plane, by bus, by car, on foot, on the plane, in the car.

rules.formula: During + festival, people + simple present verb
examples: During Nowruz, Iranians wear clean clothes and visit relatives.
On Yalda Night, families eat pomegranates and read Hafez poems.

rules.structure: Time clauses with before and after
examples: Before the New Year, we clean our houses.
After the ceremony, people recite the national anthem.

rules: Order events chronologically: preparation before the event, main celebration rituals, and concluding activities.

vocab_development.rules: bake special cookies, set the Haft-Seen table, watch fireworks, sing the national anthem, exchange gifts, hold a ceremony.
examples: set the table
sing the anthem

see_also.topic: Capitalization in National and Religious Holidays
see_also.rules: Nowruz, Yalda Night, Eid-e-Fitr, Islamic New Year.

lessons.title: Services
lessons.theme: Public services, post office, police, bank

grammar_details.focus: Asking for Public Services & Location Directions

rules.formula: Where can I + verb? -> You can go to + facility
examples: Where can I send this letter? You can go to the post office.
Where can I get emergency help? Call the police or fire station.

rules.formula: Go straight, turn left, turn right, it's next to / opposite to...
examples: Turn right on Azadi Street. The bank is on your left.

rules: Filling out postal forms: Sender name, Receiver name, Postal code, Address.

vocab_development.rules: post office, police station, fire department, central bank, hospital, emergency room, library, city hall.
examples: post office
fire department

rules.formula: Subject + past verb (watched, listened, went, saw)
examples: I watched the news last night.
He sent an email to his teacher yesterday.

rules.formula: Did + Subject + base verb? -> Yes, Subject did. / No, Subject didn't.
examples: Did you surf the internet yesterday? Yes, I did.
Did he read the morning newspaper? No, he didn't.

rules.formula: What did you watch? / When did you send it?
examples: What did you watch on TV? I watched a documentary about nature.

writing_skills.topic: Past Narrative Paragraph (What I Did Yesterday)
rules: Use past time markers: yesterday, last night, two days ago, last week, in 1399.
Ensure all verbs in the past narrative maintain past tense consistency.

vocab_development.rules: newspaper, magazine, television, interview, website, internet, text message, report, journalist, program.
examples: watch the news
send a text message

see_also.rules: /t/ after voiceless sounds (watched, worked), /d/ after voiced sounds (played, listened), /id/ after /t/ and /d/ (visited, needed).

grammar_details.focus: Talking About Past Accidents & Physical Injuries

rules.formula: What happened? / How did you hurt your ...?
examples: What happened? I fell down and hurt my knee.
How did he break his arm? He fell off his bicycle yesterday.

rules.structure: First aid and treatment in the past
rules.formula: Subject + went / called / put + treatment noun
examples: The paramedic bandaged his wound.
The ambulance arrived five minutes after the accident.

rules: Structure: 1) What occurred and where; 2) Injury description; 3) First aid treatment and medical recovery.

vocab_development.topic: Accidents, Body Injuries, and First Aid
vocab_development.rules: accident, injury, crash, hurt, cut, break, wound, bandage, plaster, emergency, paramedic, ambulance, treatment.
examples: hurt a knee
call an ambulance

see_also.topic: Irregular Past Forms of Injury Verbs
see_also.rules: hurt -> hurt (no change), cut -> cut (no change), break -> broke, fall -> fell, bleed -> bled.

passages.title: Talking about Personalities
passages.content: Nima: 'Who is your new English teacher, Ali?' Ali: 'His name is Mr. Karimi. He is very patient and knowledgeable.' Nima: 'What about your classmates?' Ali: 'Most of them are kind and helpful. Reza is very clever and hardworking, and Omid is brave and cheerful.'

passages.title: A Great Friend
passages.content: My best friend is Reza. He has a wonderful personality. He is generous, patient, and polite to everyone. Whenever classmates face difficult homework problems, Reza helps them kindly. Having loyal and honest friends makes school life enjoyable.

passages.title: Booking a Trip to Mashhad
passages.content: Travel Agent: 'Good morning, can I help you?' Customer: 'Yes, please. We are traveling to Mashhad next Thursday.' Travel Agent: 'How many passengers are traveling?' Customer: 'Four passengers. We prefer to travel by train.' Travel Agent: 'Here are your train tickets. Have a safe and pleasant journey!'

passages.title: Traveling Around Iran
passages.content: Traveling is an exciting way to learn about different cultures and historical cities. Every year, millions of Iranian families travel during Nowruz and summer holidays. Some travelers prefer airplanes for speed, while others enjoy scenic train journeys across mountains and plains. Traveling connects families and creates sweet memories.

passages.title: Talking about Nowruz Rituals
passages.content: Carlos: 'What festival are Iranians celebrating in spring, Sina?' Sina: 'We are celebrating Nowruz, the ancient Iranian New Year.' Carlos: 'What do families do during Nowruz?' Sina: 'We clean our homes, set the beautiful Haft-Seen table, wear clean clothes, and visit our grandparents and relatives.'

passages.title: Iranian Festivals and Traditions
passages.content: Iran has ancient festivals that celebrate nature, friendship, and family bonds. Nowruz marks the beginning of spring and the renewal of nature. Families gather around the Haft-Seen table to wish for health, happiness, and peace. Another celebrated festival is Yalda Night, where families stay together on the longest night of winter, eating watermelon and reciting poems of Hafez.

passages.title: Inquiring about Public Services
passages.content: Tourist: 'Excuse me, where can I send these postcards to my family?' Citizen: 'There is a central post office two blocks down on Hafez Street, next to the national bank.' Tourist: 'Thank you! Is it open in the afternoon?' Citizen: 'Yes, it is open until four o'clock. You can buy stamps there easily.'

passages.title: Services in Our City
passages.content: Every modern city provides essential public services for its citizens. Fire departments protect buildings from dangerous fires. Police stations ensure safety in streets and neighborhoods. Post offices deliver letters and packages to all parts of the country. Knowing emergency numbers and respecting public service workers is important for all citizens.

passages.title: Discussing the Evening News
passages.content: Father: 'Did you watch the eight o'clock news on television last night, Ali?' Ali: 'Yes, Dad. I watched a fascinating report about Iranian young scientists.' Father: 'What did they invent?' Ali: 'They designed a solar water pump for farms in dry desert areas. It was very interesting!'

passages.title: The Role of Media in Daily Life
passages.content: Media plays a significant role in modern society by providing news, education, and entertainment. In the past, people only read printed newspapers and listened to the radio. Today, the internet and television deliver immediate news from around the world. We can learn about scientific discoveries, global events, and cultural achievements through reliable media.

passages.title: After a Minor Bicycle Accident
passages.content: Mother: 'What happened to your knee, Farhad?' Farhad: 'I rode my bicycle in the park and slipped on wet leaves.' Mother: 'Did you hurt your arm, too?' Farhad: 'No, but my knee bled a little. The park paramedic washed the cut and put a clean bandage on it.' Mother: 'You should always wear a helmet and knee pads when cycling.'

passages.title: First Aid and Safety Rules
passages.content: Accidents happen unexpectedly, so learning basic first aid rules is essential for everyone. When a minor injury occurs, washing the cut with clean water and applying an adhesive plaster prevents infection. In serious emergencies, bystanders should remain calm and immediately call an ambulance on 115. Observing road safety rules and wearing protective gear saves human lives.
